q-214597.worked_solution:
We start by sketching the two intervals $(-1,2)$ and $[0,3)$ separately:

q-101840.problem: Find the intersection of intervals $[1,8)\cap (4,8].$ Express the result as an inequality.
q-101840.worked_solution:
We start by sketching the two intervals $[1,8)$ and $(4,8]$ separately:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/63a236a899eff365f7964a182690470011cbee2f393586fb3a673e5332b7346e.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/9b2db1951a30f71c8635e0daec81ae6931e28c2c44489952c65e10d4c95ea549.png)

The intersection $[1,8)\cap (4,8]$ represents the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/f59e4645230b48b89fb445fd3cb586516361848418e2d287e6d208c97d9dcc00.png)

Thus, $[1,8)\cap (4,8]=(4,8).$ This corresponds to the inequality $4<x<8.$

b
[2,3)

[3,5)
d
(2,3]
e
(2,3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by sketching the solutions to the two inequalities separately:

The common set of values consists of the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

Therefore, the common set of values is (3,5].

q-28909.name: Question 7
q-28909.problem: Which of the following inequalities corresponds to the intersection $(-\infty ,0)\cap (-4,\infty )\cap (-4,0]?$
q-28909.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the intervals, we graph the separate intervals on a number line and find where they overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/675114239d8d7f94928fa7914d23bb9fb81579624ae8a392aa9fde8b2df643cd.png)

Thus, $(-\infty ,0)\cap (-4,\infty )\cap (-4,0]=(-4,0).$ This corresponds to the inequality

$$
-4<x<0.
$$
